name: seo-try-keywords
label: SEO - Try New Keywords
desc: The bet manager of a two-loop SEO system: opens one cheap new-keyword bet a week, scores every open bet on the daily series, and issues the day-7 SCALE / LEAVE verdicts that earn its companion engine loops.
description:
Set up the BET MANAGER of a two-loop SEO system — it owns the edges of the emerging-keyword lifecycle: find a bet, open it with one seed article, score it daily-series-honest, issue the day-7 SCALE / LEAVE verdict, and hand winners to its companion engine loop ("SEO - Scale Proven Keywords"). Set THIS loop up first: the engine's earn-the-engine gate requires a verdict this loop produces, so on a new site the bet manager runs for weeks before any engine exists. Distilled from two live production loops. Setup is a guided conversation — confirm each step with me before creating the loop; never create a blind loop.

## Step 1 — Search Console, with the date dimension
- Verify a script or CLI on this machine returns query-dim, page-dim, and DATE-dim rows for the site's sc-domain property, and run it once by hand before creating anything. The date dimension is non-negotiable: the whole scoring doctrine is the DAILY series — never a trailing window (a trailing average once reported "SCALE, confirmed" across seven straight days of decline). Zero-impression days report position 0 and are excluded; a failed read is reported MISSING, never written as 0.

## Step 2 — The ledger, the archetypes, the funnel
- Create the bet ledger — one line per bet: term · one-line thesis · opened date · seed PR · verdict · verdict date. It is the single source of truth the engine's gate reads.
- Name winning archetypes and proven losers from ≥90 days of GSC page data. No history yet? Leave archetypes EMPTY and route every candidate through the approval lane until real click data exists — never invent archetypes from theory.
- Name the funnel (the reader's next step after any seed article) — without it the written CTA test cannot run.
- Set the open-bet cap (default 2 — more open bets than your human can merge seed PRs for is batch-crank) and the cadence: weekly, firing before your weekly review so the scorecard is fresh when you read it.

## Step 3 — The run doctrine (hard rules)
- Strict order: SCORE first, MINE second — a run never opens a new bet while it owes a verdict on an old one. Part A scores every tracked term on the daily series (3-day median vs alert bands; family growth is NOT health while the head falls) and issues day-7 verdicts: SCALE (recommend spawning an engine — never spawn it yourself; the human ticks it), LEAVE (record the one-line lesson; the seed page stays live), or ONE borderline extension — a second borderline is a LEAVE. The report files BEFORE the long mining research, so a reclaimed run never loses the week's scoring.
- Part B (mining) is gated by the open-bet cap, owed verdicts, and unmerged seed PRs — and ships at most ONE seed a week through two lanes: the archetype lane (autonomous PR off origin/main) or the approval lane (draft-pending-approval, the human approves). Zero is valid; thin seeds pollute the archetype evidence every future bet is judged against.
- Never edit a tracked term's pages after the seed — that is engine/enrichment territory. Never scale, kill, or extend silently. Never commit to main. Never fabricate a metric. Emerging-but-unsearchable goes to the watchlist with a drop-dead date, never to a seed article.

## Step 4 — Author the task file from the template + dashboard
- Fetch the full task-file TEMPLATE at <server-url>/api/skill/references/templates/seo-try-keywords/reference.md (on demand — it is not in this prompt), copy it into the loop folder as the task file, fill every <FILL: …> with the answers above, and delete its SETUP block. Optionally attach the marker-gate pre-run workflow so a half-configured loop refuses to run.
- Dashboard at creation: declare the template's state metrics — open_bets, bets_alerting, verdicts_issued, seed_prs_unmerged, watchlist_items — as a chart plus a bet-board kanban, so runs report them from day one.
